title: Conservatives call on Diana Fox Carney to testify to Parliament about ocean envoy role
html:
Diana Fox Carney, wife of Prime Minister Mark Carney, attends a high-level pledging event for the OceanEye International Alliance in support of the Global Ocean Observing System (GOOS), on the sidelines of the the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) at the UN headquarters on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026.Justin Tang/The Canadian Press

The Conservatives are calling on Prime Minister Mark Carney’s wife to testify to Parliament on her role as ocean envoy, arguing the government is not being transparent about her responsibilities and possible lobbying concerns.

“If somebody goes and lobbies her in her position as special envoy to oceans, is that recorded anywhere?” Manitoba MP Branden Leslie said Thursday. “There is a certain element of transparency, considering who she’s going home with at the end of the night.”

In September, Fisheries Minister Joanne Thompson announced that Carney’s wife, Diana Fox Carney, will serve as Canada’s “ocean envoy.”

A departmental news release said Fox Carney is expected to “advance Canada’s leadership by connecting ocean conservation, climate action, Indigenous leadership, economic resilience and maritime security.”

The role has already taken Fox Carney to Iqaluit and a climate conference in Turkey, and she will chair a major conference in Halifax next spring.

“If you’re going to be travelling abroad and speaking on behalf of Canadians, you have to be answerable to Canadians,” Leslie said.

The Conservatives say Canadians should know more about Fox Carney’s priorities, what authority she has been given to shape policy, and how her staffing and travel are funded.

MP Jonathan Rowe tabled a motion Thursday at the House environment committee requesting that Fox Carney appear before the committee to explain her mandate.

He argued others with more expertise in oceans could have been appointed to the role, than Carney’s spouse. “Did he wake up one morning and say, ‘This would be a great thing for my wife to get out of the house’?”

Liberals adjourned debate on the motion.

Newfoundland MP Clifford Small accused the Liberals of dragging out the clock on previous attempts to have Fox Carney testify. He said there have been five attempts to vote on the matter at the House fisheries committee and that all were blocked when government MPs voted to adjourn.

“It’s an affront to democracy,” Small told reporters. “We just want to find out what her role is all about, who’s going to be influencing her, and what are the impacts going to be on those that earn their living and rely on the ocean.”

Other envoy roles have involved cabinet orders spelling out the terms and compensation involved. Carney appointed former MP Chrystia Freeland as special representative for the reconstruction of Ukraine through a cabinet order. Foreign service staff testified in Parliament on how many people supported Freeland in the role and how Ottawa paid for her travel.

Leslie said Conservatives don’t want to see anyone named to a role in government without adequate transparency and the Carney family connection adds to their concerns.

“Regardless of who is in that position, the environment committee and/or the fisheries committee would certainly be inviting that individual to come and explain their new mandate,” he said.

Leslie noted Fox Carney held previous roles at think tanks that touch on environmental issues, and the government is now looking at working with firms on oceans projects worth millions of dollars. He said her past work raises lobbying concerns, considering she does not seem to have any legal requirement to report whom she meets.

Carney’s office has not yet provided a response to the issues the Conservatives raised Thursday but has said Fox Carney’s role is unpaid. The position appears to be outside the scope of federal conflict-of-interest rules.

Ethics Commissioner Konrad von Finckenstein told the House fisheries committee last month that Fox Carney’s appointment was a cabinet decision and he did not see a conflict in her hosting a conference next year.

Leslie also noted that previous prime ministers’ spouses have generally done charitable works, citing the example of Stephen Harper’s wife Laureen advocating for animal welfare. Justin Trudeau’s former spouse Sophie Grégoire focused on mental wellness.

Fox Carney has appeared on various panels in recent months, including a Toronto event last month on the challenges of regulating online content for youth.
summary: The Conservatives say Canadians should know more about Fox Carney’s priorities
